skill.name: Plugin Settings
skill.description: Guides developers in storing per-project plugin configuration in .claude/*.local.md files using YAML frontmatter and Markdown content.
skill.summary: Document and implement local Claude Code plugin settings with frontmatter-based configuration.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation-only Bash snippets or Markdown backticks and were adjudicated as false positives. The real residual risks are the included executable shell helpers and patterns that can feed local Markdown settings content back into agent prompts or terminal sessions.

remediation.issue: Local Markdown body content can be reused as prompt text.
remediation.suggestion: Document a strict trust boundary: only user-authored settings bodies may be used as prompts, and tools should ask for confirmation before feeding body text back to Claude.

remediation.issue: Settings values can influence terminal session actions.
remediation.suggestion: Whitelist allowed tmux session names, sanitize displayed text, and never allow settings content to send executable keystrokes.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts use ad hoc shell parsing for Markdown frontmatter.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a real YAML parser for complex settings, whitelist field names, validate types, and reject unexpected paths before reading files.

remediation.issue: Executable examples may be copied into hooks without review.
remediation.suggestion: Mark scripts as opt-in examples, document required permissions, and include comments that they should be adapted before production use.

content.value_statement: Plugin authors need a simple way to store project-specific settings without committing private configuration. This skill explains a local Markdown settings pattern with frontmatter, validation, examples, and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Explains the .claude/plugin-name.local.md convention for local plugin settings.
Shows YAML frontmatter and Markdown body layouts for configuration and state.
Provides Bash hook examples for reading enabled flags, modes, and size limits.
Includes scripts to validate settings files and extract frontmatter fields.
Documents gitignore, restart, permissions, and default-value practices.
Compares command, hook, and agent usage patterns for plugin settings.
limitations: Bash examples use grep, sed, and awk rather than a complete YAML parser.
The skill is guidance and examples, not a packaged settings runtime.
Claude Code hook changes still require a restart to take effect.
Local Markdown body content must be trusted before being used as prompt text.

use_cases.title: Add Project Settings to a Plugin
use_cases.description: Define a local settings file format, document defaults, and read simple options from hooks or commands.

use_cases.title: Validate Local Configuration Files
use_cases.description: Check frontmatter structure, required markers, boolean fields, and Markdown body presence before relying on settings.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent State
use_cases.description: Store lightweight task state, coordinator names, and iteration counters in a project-local file.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple local settings file pattern for my Claude Code plugin. Include enabled, mode, defaults, and restart guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Hook Parsing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add safe frontmatter parsing to a Claude Code hook that reads enabled, strict_mode, and max_file_size from a local settings file.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plugin settings schema and propose validation rules for booleans, numeric limits, paths, and missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Design Stateful Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a state file pattern for a multi-step Claude Code workflow. Include trust boundaries, atomic updates, prompt-safety rules, and cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: I need local settings for a plugin that can be enabled or disabled per project.
output_examples.output: A recommended .claude plugin settings file layout, default values, gitignore entry, and restart instructions.

output_examples.input: My hook needs to reject writes over a configured size limit.
output_examples.output: A parsing plan that reads max_file_size, validates it as a number, applies a safe default, and denies oversized writes.

output_examples.input: I want an agent workflow to keep iteration state in a local file.
output_examples.output: A state-file design with counters, completion criteria, atomic updates, and warnings about trusted prompt content.

best_practices: Keep local settings files out of version control and document the gitignore rule.
Validate every parsed value before using it in paths, shell commands, or hook decisions.
Treat Markdown body content as untrusted unless the user explicitly created it.
anti_patterns: Do not parse complex YAML with fragile shell commands when a real parser is available.
Do not feed settings body text back to an agent without trust checks and user consent.
Do not let settings choose arbitrary file paths, terminal sessions, or shell arguments.

faq.question: What file format does this skill recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends .claude/plugin-name.local.md files with YAML frontmatter and optional Markdown body content.

faq.question: Are settings files meant to be committed?
faq.answer: No. They are local project files and should be excluded with .claude/*.local.md in .gitignore.

faq.question: Can hooks read these settings automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show hooks checking for the file, parsing frontmatter, and applying validated options.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a full YAML parser?
faq.answer: No. It shows shell parsing for simple fields and recommends yq for more complex YAML.

faq.question: Why do changes require a restart?
faq.answer: Claude Code hooks are loaded for the session, so changed settings may not affect hooks until restart.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: Do not treat local Markdown body content as trusted instructions unless the user created and approved it.
